# Ruby Gillis

## Overview

- **Age:** Seventeen  <sub>[v1 c26 P5](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0005)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011)</sub>
- **Status:** Deceased  <sub>[v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030)</sub>
- **Origin:** Avonlea, Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v1 c15 P8](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0008), [v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011)</sub>
- **Role:** Schoolteacher  <sub>[v1 c30 P21](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0021), [v3 c11 P4](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0004)</sub>

## Appearance

Ruby was a handsome young woman with a brilliant complexion, large blue eyes, and long, thick, golden-yellow hair worn in braids or done up. She was plump and showy in her youth, though during her final illness she became very thin and pale with a hectic, brilliant flush. She loved wearing bright colors, silk blouses, and flowers or ribbons in her hair.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011), [v1 c15 P13](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0013), [v1 c28 P3](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0003), [v1 c30 P43](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0043), [v3 c2 P1](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0001), [v3 c11 P4](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0004), [v3 c11 P52](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0052), [v3 c14 P5](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0005)_

## Personality

Ruby was gay, cheerful, and good-tempered, enjoying the pleasant things of life frankly and laughing a great deal. She was deeply preoccupied with boys, flirtations, and beaus, constantly talking about her admirers. inclined to hysteria when frightened or excited, she also possessed a shallow, sentimental nature that clung desperately to earthly life. Despite her vanity, she was warm-hearted, kind, and harbored a genuine affection for her friends.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P39](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0039), [v1 c26 P21](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0021), [v2 c26 P59](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0059), [v3 c2 P1](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0001), [v3 c5 P7](../source/v03-c05.md#nw-v03-c05-p0007), [v3 c11 P53](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0053), [v3 c14 P13](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0013), [v3 c14 P23](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0023)_

## History

Ruby grew up in Avonlea and attended the local school, where she became a member of the girls' Story Club and a classmate of Anne Shirley. After finishing school, she studied at Queen's Academy alongside Anne and her friends, obtaining her teacher's license. She subsequently taught at Carmody, where she was known for her numerous flirtations and admirers. Ruby later accepted the White Sands school, but contracted a severe attack of congestion during the winter which developed into galloping consumption. Unable to teach, she returned home to Avonlea for her final summer. For months she refused to acknowledge her illness, continuing to dress up and talk gaily of her beaus. However, shortly before her death, she broke down to Anne, confessing her deep fear of dying and leaving the earthly life she loved. She died peacefully in her sleep at the age of nineteen, leaving behind a deep impression of her transformed beauty and a lingering memory among her old schoolmates.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P8](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0008), [v1 c26 P20](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0020), [v1 c30 P20](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0020), [v1 c36 P23](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0023), [v2 c26 P59](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0059), [v3 c2 P2](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0002), [v3 c11 P4](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0004), [v3 c11 P52](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0052), [v3 c14 P2](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0002), [v3 c14 P11](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0011), [v3 c14 P17](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0017), [v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030), [v3 c14 P31](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0031)_

## Quotes

> I can’t do it, Grandma. I don’t really know if I can eat anything. I feel as if there was a dreadful lump in my throat. I’d have cried coming home from school if Jake Donnell hadn’t been watching me. I believe I will cry after I go to bed. It wouldn’t show on my eyes tomorrow, would it?  <sub>[v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011)</sub>

> I’m not afraid but that I’ll go to heaven, Anne. I’m a church member. But—it’ll be all so different. I think—and think—and I get so frightened—and—and—homesick. Heaven must be very beautiful, of course, the Bible says so—but, Anne, it won’t be what I’ve been used to.  <sub>[v3 c14 P13](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0013)</sub>

> I want to live. I want to live like other girls. I—I want to be married, Anne—and—and—have little children. You know I always loved babies, Anne. I couldn’t say this to any one but you. I know you understand. And then poor Herb—he—he loves me and I love him, Anne. The others meant nothing to me, but he does—and if I could live I would be his wife and be so happy. Oh, Anne, it’s hard.  <sub>[v3 c14 P17](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0017)</sub>
